```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

How does an ownership change interact with firms' roles? This guide compares
sequential Stackelberg leadership with a simultaneous core-fringe game. Both are
noncooperative; neither is the PLE coordinated coalition. Use
**coordination 0.1.0** and compatible **antitrust >= 0.99.43**. The illustrative
Logit inputs use currency per unit and inside quantity per period.

| Game | Strategic choices |
|---|---|
| Stackelberg | Leaders anticipate strategic followers' responses |
| Core-fringe | Core firms choose simultaneously; fringe products use atomistic conditions |
| PLE | A coordinating coalition faces incentive constraints and a best-responding fringe |

## A leader and its followers

Use the qualified name `coordination::stackelberg()`: antitrust exports a
different legacy quantity-model function with the same name. Ownership and role
arguments below are **firm IDs**. Shares are unconditional quantity shares,
summing to .80, with a positive outside share .20 and `normIndex = NA`.

```{r stackelberg-scenario}
library(antitrust)
library(coordination)
prices <- c(10, 12, 11, 9)
shares <- c(.25, .20, .18, .17)
margins <- c(.40, .38, .35, .25)
owner <- c("A", "B", "C", "D")
leader_fit <- coordination::stackelberg(prices = prices, shares = shares,
  margins = margins, ownerPre = owner, leadersPre = "A",
  conduct = "bertrand", insideSize = 1000)
leader_merger <- coordination::stackelberg_simulate(leader_fit,
  ownerPost = c("A", "A", "C", "D"), leadersPost = "A")
knitr::kable(data.frame(product = leader_fit@labels,
  price_pre = antitrust::calcPrices(leader_fit, TRUE),
  price_post = antitrust::calcPrices(leader_merger, FALSE),
  q_pre = antitrust::calcQuantities(leader_fit, TRUE),
  q_post = antitrust::calcQuantities(leader_merger, FALSE)), digits = 3)
coordination::stackelberg_residuals(leader_merger, preMerger = FALSE)$max
```

Firm A acquires B's product and remains the explicit post-merger leader. Read
price and q columns as levels; follower responses are part of the sequential
solution. The residual reports the largest reduced leader/follower FOC error,
not a probability or proof of a unique global equilibrium. Demand and baseline
costs remain calibrated from the original fit in `stackelberg_simulate()`.

## A simultaneous core and atomistic fringe

The next baseline has A and B in the strategic core. Its merger creates one
core firm; C and D remain fringe. An ownership change requires the intended
post-core IDs explicitly.

```{r core-fringe-scenario}
core_fit <- coordination::core_fringe(prices = prices, shares = shares,
  margins = margins, ownerPre = owner, corePre = c("A", "B"),
  conduct = "bertrand", insideSize = 1000)
core_merger <- coordination::core_fringe_simulate(core_fit,
  ownerPost = c("A", "A", "C", "D"), corePost = "A")
knitr::kable(data.frame(product = core_fit@labels,
  price_pre = antitrust::calcPrices(core_fit, TRUE),
  price_post = antitrust::calcPrices(core_merger, FALSE),
  q_pre = antitrust::calcQuantities(core_fit, TRUE),
  q_post = antitrust::calcQuantities(core_merger, FALSE)), digits = 3)
coordination::core_fringe_residuals(core_merger, preMerger = FALSE)$max
```

Compare this scenario within its own fitted baseline. A core-fringe fringe
product does not have the same strategic objective as a Stackelberg follower.
Consequently the two tables are not merely alternative solver outputs for an
identical game. Treat fringe influence on aggregate demand conditions as
negligible only when the market evidence and the intended approximation justify
it. This fringe uses an atomistic **MonCom** condition, which can retain a markup;
it does not generically impose price equal to marginal cost. Choose strategic
Stackelberg followers when their reactions are part of what leaders anticipate.

In this fixed-cost core-fringe example C/D keep prices 11/9 while their quantities
rise; strategic Stackelberg followers' prices also respond in their own scenario.
That contrast follows these calibrated objectives, not a universal prediction
that fringe prices never change. Fractional-control matrices are not substitutes
for the required firm-ID vectors.

```{r role-residual-check, include=FALSE}
stopifnot(coordination::stackelberg_residuals(leader_merger, FALSE)$max < 1e-5,
          coordination::core_fringe_residuals(core_merger, FALSE)$max < 1e-5)
```

## CES changes share and size units

CES uses unconditional **revenue shares**, inside **expenditure**, and a positive
outside-good price. In this example `gamma = 3` supplies the structural
elasticity. Omitting it calibrates from usable observed margins, a different
input assumption.

```{r ces-variant}
ces_fit <- coordination::stackelberg(demand = "ces", conduct = "bertrand",
  gamma = 3, prices = prices, shares = shares, margins = margins,
  ownerPre = owner, leadersPre = "A", insideSize = 1000, priceOutside = 1)
antitrust::calcShares(ces_fit, revenue = TRUE)
```

| Demand/market | Conduct | Price domain |
|---|---|---|
| Output Logit | Bertrand or Cournot | Positive |
| Input Logit | Bertrand or Cournot | Positive, or explicit `price_domain = "real"` |
| Output CES | Bertrand or Cournot | Positive |
| Input CES | Unsupported | — |

This table applies to both role families. Input Logit real-domain support allows
finite zero or negative **counterfactual rates**; constructor observations and
all demand-domain conditions still apply. At zero/signed rates, proportional
margins or revenue shares may be undefined. Use dollar markdowns
`antitrust::calcMargins(object, level=TRUE)` and inspect the diagnostic
attributes rather than interpreting missing normalized measures as zero.

## Limits and next reading

Keep explicit roles after changing ownership. These APIs do not automatically
add products or infer leader/core identities from a merged firm name. Cost shocks
and active-product selections have their documented meanings; they do not
recalibrate demand. Reduced FOC checks assess numerical stationarity within the
model and its scale, not the economic validity of the role assignment.

See `?coordination::stackelberg`, `?core_fringe`, the
[PLE identification guide](price-leadership.html) ([source](https://github.com/luciu5/coordination/blob/main/vignettes/price-leadership.Rmd)), and the
[model reference](https://github.com/luciu5/coordination/blob/main/doc/coordination-model-reference.md).
Tariff promotion is provided by trade under its separate physical/effective-cost
contract; direct retention arguments in these native games require the matching
effective-cost treatment described in help.
